audience.value: Students beginning Rocq, with basic programming experience but no assumed Gallina or proof-tactic experience.

communication_intent.value: Teach Gallina data modeling and computation first, then develop elementary proof skills through worked examples, code/results, proof states, and student practice while covering the key technical content of Basics.html.

audience_outcome.value: Students can define inductive data and structurally recursive functions; distinguish computed booleans from propositions; use intros, simpl, reflexivity, rewrite, and destruct; explain the grading-policy and binary-number examples; and check homework assumptions.

core_message.value: Programs compute over inductively defined data; proofs establish their general properties by computation, rewriting, and exhaustive case analysis.

delivery_context.value: Primarily an instructor-led English course lecture with live code walkthroughs and short exercises; secondarily slides for independent review. Follow the 4:3 academic style of output_R1.pdf and reserve dedicated areas for code and results/proof states.

artifact_afterlife.value: Editable PPTX course material for student revision and instructor reuse, grounded in the supplied Basics chapter.

content_divergence.value: Summarize and reorganize for student understanding; choose examples appropriately while retaining all important concepts and technical details.
